title: The tiny relay setting that blacked out thirty million people
hook: One small switch setting left thirty million people in the dark.
summary: On November 9, 1965, a protective relay near Niagara Falls set too low tripped and triggered a cascade that blacked out the Northeast US and Ontario.
sources: Wikipedia: Northeast blackout of 1965 (Nov 9, 1965; about 30 million people; Sir Adam Beck Station No. 2 relay set too low; up to 13 hours)
Federal Power Commission report 'Prevention of Power Failures' (1967) on the cause and cascade; led to reliability councils and NERC's predecessor

lines.text: One small switch setting left thirty million people in the dark.
lines.caps: One small *setting | left *thirty million | people in the *dark

lines.text: It was rush hour on November ninth, nineteen sixty-five.
Near Niagara Falls, a safety relay had been set too low.
lines.caps: Near *Niagara Falls, | a safety *relay | set too *low

lines.text: A small rise in demand tripped it, and one power line shut off.
lines.caps: A small *rise | *tripped it, | one *power line | shut *off

lines.text: Its power spilled onto other lines, which overloaded and shut off too.
Within minutes, the grid collapsed across the Northeast and Ontario.
Power took up to thirteen hours to return.
Engineers then built councils to stop one failure spreading.

post.caption:
One badly set relay near Niagara Falls took down the lights from New York to Ontario.
What tiny thing do you think could still break a whole system today?
